how_sub: Simple, and you can always see why.
agent_intake: Reads your message or screenshot, finds numbers, links and what it asks of you. Spots tricks aimed at fooling AI.
agent_planner: Decides what to look up for this message.
agent_investigator: Searches scam reports, public alerts and real operator messages, and links your message to known campaigns.
agent_critic: Re-checks every number itself and argues the message is genuine. Nothing weak gets through.
agent_reporter: Writes your answer in plain English or French, with safe next steps from official channels only.
alerts_sub: Published by fraud analysts from campaigns that people's checks helped uncover. Each alert is signed: you can verify it really comes from CheckAm.
analyst_title: For fraud teams, CERT and fact-checkers
analyst_sub: Every check feeds a campaign graph. Analysts see linked reports, alerts and citizen checks, read an evidence dossier and publish signed alerts.
install_sub: Install it like an app. On Android, from any SMS or WhatsApp message, tap Share → CheckAm. On any phone, copy the message and tap Paste, or forward it to @checkam_bot on Telegram.
install_ios: On iPhone: in Safari tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. To check a message, copy it and tap Paste, send a screenshot, or add CheckAm to your Share menu.
footer_data: Built on Stop Arnaque 237, an open dataset of real scams reported in Cameroon.

ios_share_title: Add CheckAm to your iPhone Share menu (once, 1 minute)
ios_share_steps: Open the Shortcuts app and tap + to make a new shortcut.
Tap the ⓘ button and turn on Show in Share Sheet. Under Receive, keep only Text.
Add the action URL Encode. It encodes the Shortcut Input.
Add the action Open URLs and type https://checkam.me/?text= then insert URL Encoded Text right after it.
Name it CheckAm. Now in Messages, WhatsApp or Mail: press and hold a message, tap Share, then CheckAm.

meta_title: CheckAm: check a message before you send
meta_desc: Paste or forward a suspicious message. CheckAm compares it with real scam reports and tells you what to do. Free, in English and French.
privacy_intro: What CheckAm does with what you send.
privacy_p1: You do not need an account, a name or a phone number to check a message.
privacy_p2: The message with phone numbers turned into codes and PINs removed, the verdict and the kind of scam, the language, whether it was text or a screenshot, the links in it, and the time. Your screenshots, your name and your phone number are not saved.
privacy_p3: CheckAm uses AI services to read a message and write the answer. They receive the message with phone numbers already turned into codes and PINs removed. A screenshot is sent as an image so its text can be read, and it is not kept.
privacy_p4: Saved records let CheckAm spot the same scam going round and warn people sooner. Because numbers are codes, a record cannot be traced back to your phone. A record is kept for {keep} months. After that it is counted into anonymous monthly totals and moved to a compressed archive that only the CheckAm administrator can open, and the archive is deleted after another {archive} months.
privacy_p5: A share link shows the verdict and a signed proof that CheckAm gave it, never the message. If you tell us an answer looks wrong, an analyst may read the saved record to correct it.
privacy_p4_none: Saved records let CheckAm spot the same scam going round and warn people sooner. Because numbers are codes, a record cannot be traced back to your phone. A record is kept for {keep} months, then it is counted into anonymous monthly totals and deleted.
